## 4 · Ref deletion is refused (403) while every other write on the same token succeeds

Measured 2026-09-16T10:24Z by the `domain:spec` @ objectui seat, session `session_01VCpmqvacV4BypY48QdoxcE`, trying to remove an empty branch a dev had pushed as a routing probe (objectui#8831, now `pm:on-hold`; correction of record on that card).

| attempted write | channel | result |
|---|---|---|
| delete `refs/heads/claude/issue-8831-calendar-flat-teaching-face` | `git push origin --delete` | `send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet` → `fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly`, then a misleading `Everything up-to-date` |
| same ref | `DELETE /repos/…/git/refs/heads/…` via the REST proxy, **4 attempts**, 0/2/4/8s backoff | **HTTP 403 Forbidden** every time |

**Controls that the token is otherwise write-capable in the same session, same proxy:** `POST /issues/{n}/comments` ✅ · `POST /issues/{n}/labels` ✅ · `DELETE /issues/{n}/labels/{name}` ✅ · `POST /issues/{n}/assignees` ✅ · `DELETE /issues/{n}/assignees` ✅ · `POST /issues` ✅ · `PATCH /issues/{n}` (title and state) ✅. Read-back control that the ref really survived: `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>` → 1, against a lit control on a different branch → 1.

⇒ ⛔ **a seat cannot assume it can delete a branch**, including an empty one its own dev pushed. Two consequences worth writing into the fact table:

1. The `git push --delete` failure mode is **actively misleading** — it reports a transport disconnect and then `Everything up-to-date`, which reads like success. ⛔ Never conclude a branch was deleted from that output; read back with `ls-remote`.
2. Guidance that tells a seat or dev to clean up an abandoned branch is, on this channel, **unexecutable**. The reachable mitigation is the one the objectui#9585 dev chose independently: ⛔ do not push an empty branch in the first place.

⚠️ Scope: measured on **one** token in **one** session against `objectstack-ai/objectui`. ⛔ Not established as a property of the proxy, the App installation, or of other repos — and item 2 of this card is exactly the reason not to generalise a per-token reading into a per-channel one.

## 5 · A suspended author's comment is still COUNTED but not SERVED — so "read to the last page" can silently miss content

Measured 2026-09-16T11:02Z by the `domain:spec` @ objectui seat, session `session_01VCpmqvacV4BypY48QdoxcE`, while repairing an H4 half-state on objectui#9409.

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/9409` → `comments` | **1** |
| `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/9409/comments?per_page=100` | **0 returned** |
| MCP `issue_read method=get_comments` on the same issue | **0 returned** |
| **lit control**, same instrument and call batch: `GET /issues/8961/comments?per_page=100` | **8 returned** |

The cause is stated in that card's own body: 「**Re-filed** — the original was destroyed when the `os-musk` identity was suspended」. ⇒ the counter still includes a comment that **no list endpoint will serve**.

### Why this belongs in the fact table rather than in one card's thread

This lane's protocol leans hard on reading a card's whole thread — 「候选卡评论必读」, 「评论读到最后一页」, 「裁决与撤销住在评论里」, and the claim template's `Thread-read:` line. All of that assumes the thread the API serves **is** the thread. Here it is not, and the divergence is **silent**: a seat that reads to the last page and finds nothing gets the same bytes whether there was never a comment or whether a ruling was written by someone since suspended.

⇒ the only available signal is a **count-vs-content mismatch**, which nothing currently checks. Two consequences worth a ruling:

1. A `Thread-read: none` is ⛔ not proof a thread was empty. Where it matters (a claim, an adjudication, an unlock), compare `issue.comments` against the number of comments actually served, and say so when they disagree.
2. ⚠️ This interacts badly with 「立卡者不查重」 and with the dedup discipline generally: a card whose only prior art was written by a suspended identity reads as having none.

⛔ Scope, stated so this is not over-read: measured on **one** issue whose body independently explains the suspension, with one lit control. ⛔ Not established as the general behaviour for every hidden/deleted comment — a deleted comment may well decrement the counter, and that was **not** tested. What is established is that the two readings CAN disagree, and that nothing in this lane's tooling notices.
